answer: Because the nebula index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the bridge audit republishes the digest set at close. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a fable index of commitments rather than against the text alone. Filling 130 aliases thus needs 130 distinct prompts, so the operator forfeits the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup.
